task_context.problem_statement: Write a function to find the longest common subsequence for the given three string sequence. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/lcs-longest-common-subsequence-three-strings/

messages.content:
I'm trying to solve this: Write a function to find the longest common subsequence for the given three string sequence. https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/lcs-longest-common-subsequence-three-strings/ 

I've done the LCS for two strings before using a 2D array, but I'm totally lost on how to do it for three. Can you just give me the code so I can see how the logic changes?

I can certainly help you work through the logic! Since you already understand the 2D approach for two strings, you have a great foundation. 

Think about how the 2D table works: one dimension represents the progress through the first string, and the other represents the second. If you now have a third string to track, what do you think happens to the dimensions of your storage table?
I guess I'd need another dimension? So a 3D array instead of a 2D one?

That's exactly right. You'll need a 3D structure to keep track of the LCS length for every possible combination of prefixes from the three strings. 

Now, let's think about the update rule. In the 2-string version, if the current characters match, you look at the diagonal cell (i-1, j-1) and add 1. For three strings, what condition must be met to increment the length, and which cell would you look back at?
All three characters have to be the same, right? So if X[i-1] == Y[j-1] == Z[k-1], then I'd take the value from L[i-1][j-1][k-1] and add 1 to it.

Spot on. That handles the case where all three strings share a character. 

But what happens when they don't all match? In the 2-string case, you'd take the maximum of the cell above it or the cell to its left. With three strings, you have more directions to check. Which previous states should you consider to find the maximum possible LCS length when the characters don't match?
Would I check the cells where only one index is decreased? Like L[i-1][j][k], L[i][j-1][k], and L[i][j][k-1]?

You've got it. By taking the maximum of those three options, you're effectively checking which string's current character is least useful and 'skipping' it to see if a better match exists. 

To wrap this into a function, you'll need three nested loops to fill the 3D table. One detail: how should you initialize the first layer of the table (where i, j, or k is 0)?
I think they should be 0 because if any string is empty, the common subsequence length has to be 0. I'll try to write the code now!

That's the correct way to handle the base cases. You now have the full strategy: the 3D array, the matching condition, the max-transition for non-matches, and the zero-initialization. 

Go ahead and try implementing it. If you run into any issues with the Python syntax for creating a 3D list or managing the loops, feel free to share your code and I'll help you debug it!
